records.text: Lieutenant Doren leads the rebels at their camp in the campaign against Colonel Kurzen. He explains that Kurzen’s corruption turned the rebels’ former loyalty into anger, and sent Private Thorsen back among Kurzen’s men as a covert source of intelligence. When that secret leaked, Doren suspected a traitor and later identified Merle as the betrayer. He urges the fight against Kurzen, whose defeat gives Doren hope that the rebels can survive.
A Bloodscalp warrior who bashes a foe that is casting a spell with a shield and grows enraged when badly wounded.
A Bloodscalp scout who goes into a frenzy when badly wounded.
A Bloodscalp hunter who throws weapons at foes and goes into a frenzy when badly wounded.
A Bloodscalp berserker, a direct and forceful fighter that becomes enraged when badly wounded and grows more dangerous as the fight turns against it.
A Bloodscalp witch doctor, a spellcaster who supports the Bloodscalp fighters by dropping an Earthgrab Totem in battle, and who can become enraged.
A Skullsplitter warrior, a close-range fighter who attacks with a blow called Head Crack.
A Skullsplitter hunter who fights with Thrash. Gan'zulah, in his rage, names Skullsplitter hunters among those he wants slain in revenge.
A Skullsplitter witch doctor, a spellcaster who plants an Earthgrab Totem and raises a Healing Ward in battle.
A Bloodscalp headhunter who throws weapons at an aggressor and can become enraged.
A Skullsplitter spiritchaser in Stranglethorn Vale.
A Venture Co. strip miner in Stranglethorn Vale.
A Venture Co. foreman in Stranglethorn Vale.
A Venture Co. surveyor in Stranglethorn Vale.
A Venture Co. tinkerer in Stranglethorn Vale.
A Mosh’Ogg mauler in Stranglethorn Vale who roars blunt threats to smash or crush opponents.
A Mosh'Ogg troll shaman who hurls threats at intruders and calls down Chain Lightning in battle.
A Mosh'Ogg troll lord who bellows threats at intruders and rallies himself with Battle Shout in battle.
A young Stranglethorn tiger, one of the area's wild cats. Its youth makes it a less formidable quarry than the mature tigers.
A mature Stranglethorn tiger, a stronger wild cat than the young tigers found in the region.
A Stranglethorn raptor, one of the jungle's dangerous beasts, that attacks with a savage bite. Hemet Nesingwary Jr. treats them as big game for hunters to test themselves on.
A Jungle Stalker is a cagey breed of raptor in Stranglethorn, far harder to track down than the other raptors. It attacks with a savage bite.
A wild basilisk of Stranglethorn that attacks intruders with its Crystal Gaze.
A Crystal Spine Basilisk found in Stranglethorn. It defends itself with a Crystal Gaze, turning its gaze into a threat to creatures that approach.
A Cold Eye Basilisk of Stranglethorn, dangerous to approach. It can use Crystalline Slumber to incapacitate its prey.
A lesser water elemental, a small elemental fighter that calls on a special spell once it is wounded.
A Bloodscalp axe thrower who fights at range with thrown weapons and can become enraged in battle.
A Skullsplitter axe thrower, a ranged fighter who attacks with thrown weapons.
A Bloodscalp shaman who wards itself with Lightning Shield before a fight and can become enraged in battle.
A Bloodscalp tiger, a fierce feline predator that becomes enraged when badly wounded.
A Bloodscalp beastmaster who opens a fight by throwing a weapon and can become enraged.
A Bloodscalp mystic who attacks with thrown weapons and can become enraged.
A Bloodscalp scavenger in Stranglethorn Vale.
A Mosh’Ogg warmonger in Stranglethorn Vale who roars blunt threats to smash or crush opponents.
A Mosh’Ogg spellcrafter in Stranglethorn Vale who roars blunt threats to smash or crush opponents.

Hemet Nesingwary Jr. hunts big game in Stranglethorn Vale, with King Bangalash as the coveted prize. He tests newcomers through raptor hunts and insists that locating prey is half the challenge. He teaches raptor hunting alongside Ajeck’s tiger hunting and Sir Erlgadin’s panther tracking. Hemet recalls his father’s hunts with Roon Wildmane in Desolace, considers a future expedition there, and says his father has gone farther afield seeking bigger prey.

Barnil Stonepot is one of Master Nesingwary’s hunting companions and was trusted to proofread The Green Hills of Stranglethorn. Worried after wind scattered the manuscript, Barnil seeks help recovering and organizing its chapters, and delights in the hunting stories. Preparing Nesingwary for the jungle feels more relaxing than preparing for combat, though Barnil misses glorious battlefield moments.

Ajeck Rouack is a tiger hunter with Nesingwary’s Expedition. Her father taught her tiger hunting when she was young, and she now trains others through increasingly difficult hunts, from young tigers to the fiercer elders. She describes the elder hunt as preparation for a final challenge before presenting a hunter’s mastery to Master Nesingwary.

Sir S. J. Erlgadin teaches panther hunting with the expedition led by Hemet Nesingwary Jr. He expects would-be companions to prove skill and commitment in the field, progressing from young panthers to harder prey. He challenges hunters to take Bhag’thera, an elusive panther his party has failed to catch, as the final proof that earns his respect.
Bhag’thera is a panther prowling Stranglethorn’s jungle. Erlgadin says Bhag’thera has eluded Nesingwary’s party and makes bringing back his fang the final test of panther mastery.

Sin’Dall is a tiger in Stranglethorn whom Ajeck Rouack’s hunting party has tracked for weeks. Ajeck describes her as elusive and makes finding her and returning with her paw the final test of tiger mastery.

Tethis is a raptor in Stranglethorn whom Ajeck Rouack calls wily. Hemet Nesingwary Jr. describes him as ferocious and says even he has failed to kill him; bringing back Tethis’s talon is his test of raptor mastery.
King Bangalash is a great white tiger in Stranglethorn. Hemet Nesingwary Jr. considers him the true prize of the expedition and says hunting him is the reason he came to the jungle.

Sergeant Yohwa serves Lieutenant Doren at Stranglethorn’s Rebel Camp. Facing Colonel Kurzen’s superior numbers, Yohwa advocates covert strikes and seizing remedies to keep the rebels alive. Yohwa knows many of Kurzen’s troops personally and regards them as skilled, loyal and cruel; recruits are warned that even a rest offers little safety from Kurzen.
Corporal Bluth is the camp trader at Stranglethorn’s Rebel Camp, selling goods to visitors.

Kebok is a Booty Bay trader working under Baron Revilgaz, and he treats the jungle’s dangers as costs to manage. He recruits help against Bloodscalp trolls after losing guards, arranges forged Skullsplitter tusks for the South Seas export trade, and steals Tumbled Crystals from Venture Co. geologists at Revilgaz’s direction. He sees the crystals as a threat to Revilgaz’s interests and sends samples to Head Chemist Gigglefont for analysis.

Private Thorsen serves with Lieutenant Doren’s rebels and was assigned to infiltrate Kurzen’s men as a spy. His attempt to enter Kurzen’s Compound failed, leaving him grateful for rescue and anxious to return to Doren with intelligence. He also receives goblin supplies for the rebel camp, including land mines meant to defend against Kurzen. His patrol remarks suggest a watchful, guarded soldier who reports when the area seems quiet.

Brother Nimetz investigates Colonel Kurzen's corruption, seeking troll legends and Skullsplitter magical fetishes. He remembers Kurzen as once noble and is determined to understand his fall. His studies lead him to blame Mai'Zoth and the Mind's Eye; he fears the ogre mage could corrupt others and seeks to stop that influence.
Rebel Watchmen serve as watchmen among the rebels.

Corporal Kaleb does most of the cooking at the Rebel Camp and prizes Krazek's mechanical cooking pot for the labor it saves. When it breaks, he seeks Krazek's help repairing it so he can prepare dinner. He worries about visitors' safety in Booty Bay and repeats alarming rumors about drunken sailors being taken onto goblin slave boats.
Stranglethorn Tigresses are female tigers of Stranglethorn.

Krazek is a Goblin merchant and repairer in Booty Bay, known for a distinctive line of manufactured gear. His trade depends on information as well as goods: he checks reports about hunters near the Venture Company mine and draws on contacts to investigate racer pilot Nazz Steamboil. He will make those inquiries, but signals that useful information takes time and costs something. He also repairs Krazek’s Crock Pot, adding his own eccentric improvements.
A Skullsplitter troll mystic who fights with lightning, can heal an ally with a Healing Wave, and flees to find help when badly hurt.
A Skullsplitter troll headhunter among the tribe's fighters. Gan'zulah, in his rage, names Skullsplitter headhunters among those he wants slain in revenge against Ana'thek.
A Skullsplitter troll scout in the tribe's territory who fights with Head Crack.
A Skullsplitter berserker in Stranglethorn, among the fighters Gan’zulah’s speaking head calls the fiercest of the Skullsplitters. The tribe’s chief is Ana’thek the Cruel.
A beastmaster among the Skullsplitters of Stranglethorn.

Colonel Kurzen commands his forces from the Stockpile in Stranglethorn. The rebels regard him as a brilliant, resourceful tactician whose superior numbers threaten their survival. Brother Nimetz remembers him as once noble and investigates whether troll magic explains his fall into depravity.
Malthus is a sergeant in Stranglethorn.

Mai'Zoth is an ogre mage in the Mosh'Ogg mound, known for powerful magic and feared for mind control. Brother Nimetz believes Mai'Zoth corrupted Kurzen and warns that he could influence others; Kin'weelay calls him vicious and says his magic is strong. The Mind's Eye is tied to the danger, and Kin'weelay sees stopping Mai'Zoth as the hope of saving Yenniku.
A young jungle stalker is a wild beast of the jungle.
A young Stranglethorn raptor, a juvenile beast of the region.
A Saltscale warrior may flee for help when badly hurt.
A Saltscale oracle who hurls Lightning Bolt in battle.
A Saltscale Tide Lord, a frost caster who keeps Frost Armor up and attacks with Frostbolt.
A Saltscale forager in Stranglethorn.
A Saltscale hunter in Stranglethorn.
Sharptooth Frenzy is a beast found in several areas.
Flora Silverwind is an herbalism trainer who can train visitors.
A Venture Co. lumber worker in Stranglethorn.
A Kurzen jungle fighter among Colonel Kurzen's men, who outnumber the rebels at the Rebel Camp. When badly wounded, it flees to call for help.

A Kurzen commando, part of Colonel Kurzen’s highly trained forces in Stranglethorn. Rebels describe these troops as skilled, loyal and cruel, attacking rebel soldiers in the wilderness or gathering deep in the Stockpile cave.
A Kurzen elite among Colonel Kurzen's defenders in the Stockpile cave in Stranglethorn, where the colonel commands his men.
A medicine man serving Kurzen’s forces in Stranglethorn.

A Kurzen headshrinker among the colonel’s highly trained forces in Stranglethorn. Rebels describe these troops as skilled, loyal and cruel, attacking rebel soldiers in the wilderness or gathering deep in the Stockpile cave.
A Kurzen Witch Doctor who fights with a Searing Totem.
A Kurzen Wrangler who fights with a net and may flee for help when badly hurt.
A tiger designated as a Kurzen war beast in Stranglethorn Vale.
A panther designated as a Kurzen war beast in Stranglethorn Vale.
A subchief among Colonel Kurzen’s leaders in the Stockpile. Lieutenant Doren sends fighters against the subchiefs and Kurzen in hopes of saving his band of rebels.
A Kurzen shadow hunter found in Stranglethorn Vale and Duskwood who shoots at opponents.
Ana'thek the Cruel is the chief of the Skullsplitters. Gan'zulah curses him and craves vengeance, demanding his shattered armor.
Mogh the Undying is a rare Skullsplitter Clan witchdoctor who casts spells both before a fight and during it.
Gan'zulah is the Bloodscalp Chief, a leader whose battle rage rises when he is badly hurt.
Nezzliok the Dire is the Bloodscalp Clan Witchdoctor. In battle, he casts Chain Lightning and Shock.
Grom'gol Grunts are humanoid troops stationed around Grom'gol.

Elder Stranglethorn Tigers are the hardest Stranglethorn tigers to find and the fiercest to fight, rending their foes. Ajeck Rouack of Nesingwary's Expedition uses them to test hunters nearing the final tiger challenge.
A Venture Co. miner who works in northern Stranglethorn and fights back when attacked.
A Venture Co. workboss, a company supervisor in northern Stranglethorn who fights with Battle Fury and flees for help when badly hurt.
A Venture Co. geologist in northern Stranglethorn who attacks with Lightning Bolt.
A Venture Co. mechanic in northern Stranglethorn who works in a mechanical trade and shoots at foes from range.
A Mistvale gorilla found in northern Stranglethorn. When hurt, it can answer with a special attack.
The Jungle Thunderer is a beast found in northern Stranglethorn. This animal has a special attack it can use when wounded.
A Mosh'Ogg Brute is a hostile ogre at the Mizjah Ruins. It roars blunt threats of crushing violence, such as "Me smash! You die!"
A Mosh'Ogg Witch Doctor is a hostile ogre at the Mizjah Ruins who roars the same blunt threats as the brutes and casts Curse of Weakness.
Vharr is a Superior Weaponsmith in the Grom'gol area, where he offers weapons for browsing. His title marks him as a weapons specialist among the local merchants.
Hragran is a Cloth & Leather Armor Merchant in the Grom'gol area. He offers clothing and leather armor for browsing, giving travelers a local source for those kinds of protection.
Nerrist is a Trade Goods merchant in the Grom'gol area. His listed trade goods role distinguishes his wares from the nearby weapons and armor specialists.
Uthok is a General Supplies merchant in the Grom'gol area. His role is to offer general supplies, including ammunition, to those browsing his goods.
Krakk is a superior armorer who sells his goods to visitors.
Mudduk is a superior cook who also trains pupils.

Brawn is a leatherworking trainer who resents the humans for enslaving his people. He says they hold only a small foothold for now, the humans cannot fight them off forever, and then the humans will pay: he speaks of cutting out their lying tongues for the treachery.
Thysta is a wind rider master who flies travelers to other destinations. When attacked, she calls an enraged wyvern to her aid.
Kragg is a hunter trainer, curt and impatient: he may answer "What?" or tell a visitor not to waste his time.
Ian Strom is a rogue trainer who tells those of other callings to find a trainer of their own kind. Guarded, he says visitors look like the type to watch his coin purse around.

Private Merle is a rebel soldier. Corporal Sethman's records show he was scheduled on the same patrol times as Thorsen all of last week. He curses those who attack him and swears vengeance will be his one day.
Corporal Sethman handles patrol schedules. Asked who shared patrols with Thorsen, he checks the records and says it was Private Merle, on the same patrol times all of last week.

Witch Doctor Unbagwa speaks with spirits and offers to summon Mokk the Savage after receiving a Gorilla Fang. He asks to be protected from the other gorillas while he performs the ritual, and calls out as the apes arrive, showing his own part in the dangerous ceremony.
A Zanzil Zombie casts Contagion of Rot when combat begins.
A Zanzil Hunter responds to an attack by throwing at its opponent.
A Zanzil Witch Doctor casts Shadow Bolt during combat.
A Zanzil Naga who slows foes with Hamstring and pummels them up close.

Gorlash is a sea giant associated with Booty Bay's coast. Hecklebury Smotts says Gorlash took his captain's chest to use as a snuffbox after sea giants destroyed Smotts's ship and crew. Smotts seeks the chest and describes Gorlash as wandering the coast east of Booty Bay.

Mok'rash is a giant who repeatedly taunts Captain Hecklebury Smotts and calls him out to fight at Janeiro's Point. He jokes that he may spare Smotts's crew while his brother might eat them, and says a statue is his only company. His speech shows a fixation on provoking Smotts and an awareness of his brother.
Thrashtail basilisks are found in the Booty Bay region. They are hostile creatures that lash at opponents in combat.
Ironjaw basilisks inhabit the Booty Bay region. They are hostile creatures that use a crystal flash against opponents in combat.
Scale Belly is an unusually powerful basilisk found around Booty Bay. The creature uses a crystal flash in combat.
Elder Mistvale gorillas inhabit the Mistvale area and nearby parts of the Booty Bay region. They are wild creatures that use a damaging ability when wounded in combat.
Silverback Patriarch is a large wild creature. In combat it can strike with Backhand.
King Mukla is a beast that tramples foes in combat.
A Bloodsail Raider is a humanoid member of the Bloodsail crew. In combat, raiders can use a net against their opponents.
A Bloodsail Mage is a humanoid caster of the Bloodsail crew. In combat, the mage casts Fireball.
A Bloodsail Swashbuckler is a humanoid fighter of the Bloodsail crew. Its combat behavior includes disarming and kicking opponents, and fleeing for assistance when badly hurt.
A Bloodsail Warlock is a humanoid of the Bloodsail crew.
A Bloodsail Sea Dog serving among the pirates of Stranglethorn’s coast, this sailor fights with poison.
A Bloodsail Elder Magus, this spellcaster fights with fire magic along Stranglethorn’s coast.
A naga explorer in the expedition advancing on the Holy Spring, it fights intruders with a rend attack.

Commander Aggro'gosh commands Grom'gol, the Warchief’s base camp in Stranglethorn. He puts visitors to work defending the camp’s supply route to Stonard, first against raptors near camp and then ogres ambushing caravans at Mizjah Ruins. He expects people to pull their weight and speaks of service to the Warchief as a matter of honor.

Far Seer Mok'thardin is a Horde shaman at Grom'gol whose rituals harness the jungle's magic in powerful enchantments. He asks for staged ingredients—including claws, a pristine tigress fang, gorilla sinew, and raptor feathers—for an enchanted item intended to aid the Horde and its Warchief.
Zarena Cromwind is a superior weaponsmith who sells weapons and offers repairs. Her title and services mark her as a specialist in Booty Bay's trade.
Jaquilina Dramet is a superior axecrafter who sells weapons and offers repairs. Her title identifies her specialty among Booty Bay's tradespeople.

Fin Fizracket, a Blackwater Raiders pirate in Booty Bay, is gravely ill with Stranglethorn Fever. Believing Mokk the Savage's heart is the only cure, he directs the search to Witch Doctor Unbagwa, who can summon the beast. After the heart is brought to him, Fin describes feeling stronger and waking from a strange dream, though still weak.

Fleet Master Seahorn commands the Blackwater Raiders from Booty Bay. He treats the Bloodsails as a serious threat: he sends scouts to learn their plans, has their camp infiltrated for charts and orders, and entrusts sensitive correspondence to a capable courier. With intelligence in hand, he directs an attack on Bloodsail leaders, arguing that a small skilled party can do the work without risking his whole fleet. His priorities are the fleet’s safety and Blackwater control of Booty Bay.

Deeg is a Blackwater Raider with a taste for grog and snuff. He says these are his pirate vices, and complains that Booty Bay’s herbalist has run out of snuff after a shipment was hijacked by Bloodsail Raiders. He asks an adventurer to obtain more, and is relieved to have it before he needs to ship out.

First Mate Crazz is a Blackwater Raider who handles scouting and intelligence on the Bloodsail Buccaneers. Though wary of an outsider’s offer to help, he sends a scout to investigate a cove north of Booty Bay while his crew is distracted in port. When the scout finds evidence of a planned attack, Crazz directs the report to Fleet Master Seahorn; he also receives the report from a reconnaissance of a Bloodsail camp near Booty Bay.

Whiskey Slim is a Blackwater Raiders pirate in Booty Bay who lost a crate of Pupellyverbos Port during a storm after breaking into the captain’s cargo. He fears the captain’s punishment and plainly depends on grog for courage; his joke toast keeps that thirst in view.

Dizzy One-Eye is a Blackwater Raiders pirate in Booty Bay whose enchanted glass eye is essential to his work as a lookout. A wizard enchanted it after he had already lost his sight in battle; Bloodsail Buccaneers later stole it, leaving him unable to see and worried his captain will keelhaul him. He eagerly wants it back.

Privateer Bloads is a pirate in Booty Bay who hires help for a trade in akiris reed. His friend Groy sells the valuable reed, though Bloads admits he does not know what it is used for. He asks for a bundle to be delivered to Groy in Theramore and notes the city can be dangerous for the wrong sort of visitor.

Drizzlik is a boastful Booty Bay leathercrafter who calls his work the finest and promotes his Excelsior line. He designs its boots with layered crocolisk skins and decorative accents, and is filling an order for Director Riddlevox of the Tinkers' Union to send to Undermine. He prizes fine materials, though he admits the saltwater crocolisks' decline threatens his business.

Baron Revilgaz is a Steamwheedle Cartel representative who calls himself Booty Bay's humble servant, while bluntly asking what visitors can do for him. He seeks the Stone of the Tides for his collection of ancient artifacts and relics, and investigates its curse as an obstacle to obtaining it, including seeking magical analysis of water elemental bracers. He also backs Pozzik's interest in Venture Company fuel-regulator plans.

Nimboya is a Darkspear sent from Orgrimmar to Stranglethorn to find Yenniku, his chief’s youngest son, who was lost after the tribe left with Thrall. Suspecting the Bloodscalp, he searches their shrunken heads for signs of Yenniku and is relieved when he is not among them. He also chants over skulls and sends a message against the Witherbark for betraying the Horde.

Crank Fizzlebub is a goblin entrepreneur in Booty Bay who trades in Singing Crystals and sees Venture Company mining as competition. He hires others to obtain crystals, presenting the work as an honest living even as he eagerly anticipates the profit. He also seeks Zanzil’s mind-bending mixture, recognizing its value to those who want to control others; he later reports success using it in stout. His commercial interests make him an opponent of the Venture Company in Stranglethorn.
Markel Smythe is a humanoid who gives out tasks to willing helpers.

Hecklebury Smotts remembers his career as a successful captain sailing between Booty Bay and Ratchet, and the sea giants who wrecked two of his ships and killed both crews. He wants his stolen chest and cutlass back, and speaks openly of revenge against the giants. Recovering his property brings him pleasure, though he says it only cools some of his anger.

“Sea Wolf” MacKinley is a Booty Bay debt collector who pursues gambling debts with little sympathy for what has become of his debtors. He sends help to frighten Shaky Phillipe, whom he says he can read easily at cards, then turns to cursed former debtors in the jungle and Maury's locked foot. His own attempt to open the foot fails, and he curses the obstacle.

“Shaky” Phillipe is a gambling debtor who fears Sea Wolf MacKinley’s response to his unpaid debt. He explains that he got drunk and lost his way, then asks for his payment to be returned with an assurance that he meant to repay MacKinley. When confronted with grisly giblets, he is alarmed and suspects MacKinley sent them.

Kin'weelay is a Darkspear in Grom'gol who works to save Yenniku from Zanzil. He consults jungle spirits, gathers the Mind's Eye and Singing Crystals for a ritual, and uses heads in a cauldron to hear the dead. He warns that Mai'Zoth is dangerous and fears the ogre mage may continue his reign in the spirit realm after defeat.
A Skymane gorilla found in Stranglethorn's wilds, it attacks with a trampling charge when combat begins.
Yenniku is a Darkspear hostage under Zanzil's control. When the Soul Gem is used on him, his soul can be drawn into it, leaving his body a mindless husk.

Zanzil the Outcast is an exiled witchdoctor who bends minds and controls Yenniku, according to the quest accounts. Those accounts say his leaders fear his methods, and describe him using a jungle-plant mixture on followers to suppress their will and strengthen their bodies. He dwells with followers among the Jubuwal and Aboraz ruins.

Maury "Club Foot" Wilkins is one of Sea Wolf MacKinley's debtors, with months of unpaid dues. MacKinley's account says Maury and the others were cursed and bewitched and now wander the jungle ruins; he demands Maury's Clubbed Foot as payment.

Jon-Jon the Crow is one of Sea Wolf MacKinley's debtors, whose dues have gone unpaid for months. MacKinley's account says Jon-Jon and the others were cursed and bewitched and now wander the jungle ruins; he demands Jon-Jon's Golden Spyglass as payment.

Chucky “Ten Thumbs” is one of three debtors whom “Sea Wolf” MacKinley says owe him months of unpaid debts. MacKinley reports that Chucky and the others were cursed and bewitched and now wander the jungle ruins. He seeks Chucky’s Huge Ring as part of his debt collection. Chucky also carries Zanzil’s Mixture.
Lord Sakrasis is a rare humanoid.

Catelyn the Blade is Ansirem's willful daughter, who left the prospect of a scholarly life to become a pirate with the Blackwater Raiders. Her ancient dagger, found by her father while researching Stranglethorn, is precious to her: after Duncan took it in a knife fight, she lends it for the effort against the Altar of the Tides and expects it back.
A southern sand crawler, one of the beasts of Stranglethorn Vale.

“Pretty Boy” Duncan is a Bloodsail Buccaneer who took Catelyn’s prized dagger after beating her in a knife fight. He also recruits for Fleet Master Firallon, directing prospects to the Crimson Veil for a special mission.

Fleet Master Firallon recruits adventurers aboard the Crimson Veil for a strike against Booty Bay: an aspiring honorary admiral must kill Fleet Master Seahorn and Baron Revilgaz. Returning after the task, the recruit is hailed as an Admiral of the Bloodsail Navy. Firallon also offers proper attire, recalling that Red-Eyed Ben was lost in a storm at sea.
Ironpatch is a humanoid fighter who takes a defensive stance as a fight starts and bashes foes with a shield.

Captain Keelhaul is one of the Bloodsail leaders Fleet-Master Seahorn marks for assassination, alongside Captain Stillwater and Fleet Master Firallon. He shoots, fires Exploding Shot, shouts to demoralize, and may flee for help when badly hurt.
Garr Salthoof is a humanoid fighter who charges into a fight and follows with a backhand.
Captain Stillwater is one of the Bloodsail leaders Fleet-Master Seahorn marks for assassination. He slows foes and strikes with Arcane Explosion.
Brutus is an elemental that uses spells in combat and when wounded.

Captain Smotts identifies Sprogger as his cook aboard the Smotts' Revenge and a survivor of the giants' last attack. Smotts says Sprogger can help locate Negolash; Sprogger greets those sent after the giant.
Sly Garrett deals in shady goods and sells them to visitors.
Viznik Goldgrubber is a banker who lets visitors reach their bank.
Old Man Heming sells fishing supplies.
Grarnik Goodstitch trains tailoring. He jokes that he cannot remember the saying about a stitch in time and dismisses it as stupid.
Princess Poobah speaks of being held captive by King Mukla and asks for help with her rescue. Her words convey concern about her captivity and gratitude toward those who aid her.
An elder saltwater crocolisk whose combat behavior includes casting Tendon Rip.
Narkk sells pirate supplies, asking visitors if they care to buy some piratey items.
Kelsey Yance is a cook who also sells goods.

Xizk Goodstitch is a master tailor who makes gold thread for a warlock’s enchanted bloodrobe. He asks the visitor to bring a gold bar, explains that the thread will take time, and sends it on to Menara Voidrender. He also sends greetings to Menara and Strahad, and jokes about a princess spinning the thread.
Cowardly Crosby sells tailoring supplies. His shop greeting identifies him as one of the Goodstitch brothers, giving his tailoring trade a family connection.
Mazk Snipeshot sells engineering supplies and ammunition, serving customers from his shop in the same trade as Gnaz Blunderflame.
Gnaz Blunderflame sells engineering supplies, the same trade as Mazk Snipeshot.
Rikqiz sells leatherworking supplies.
Nixxrax Fillamug sells food and drink.

Myizz Luckycatch is a fishing trainer whose own skill has limits. He points aspiring anglers toward Old Man Heming in Booty Bay for the book “The Bass and You,” and toward Nat Pagle in Dustwallow Marsh for further instruction. His advice presents him as a practical guide who knows where students can look next.

Brikk Keencraft is a blacksmithing trainer with a prickly streak when someone questions his craft. He insists that dwarves are not the only people worth trusting with an anvil, then sarcastically tells the doubter to find a dwarf instead. His sharp retort gives his instruction a touch of wounded pride.

Jaxin Chong teaches alchemy and has a business arrangement with Glyx, a pirate who supplies him. Jaxin jokes that Glyx keeps him supplied while he keeps Glyx rich, complaining in the same breath about the price of a small pouch of crushed kingsblood. His banter shows a trainer who knows the cost of keeping his work stocked and is not shy about grumbling over it.
Crazk Sparks is a fireworks merchant. His local role centers on selling fireworks, giving Booty Bay visitors a specialist in bright, explosive amusements among its traders.

Haren Kanmae is a superior bowyer who trades in goods and ammunition and can repair equipment. His services make him a practical contact for travelers relying on bows, with both supplies and maintenance tied to his craft.

Kizz Bluntstrike is a macecrafter who sells goods and repairs equipment. His trade combines weapon-making with practical upkeep, making him a useful specialist for travelers who depend on maces and need their gear maintained.
Wigcik is a superior fisherman who also offers goods for sale. His fishing title sets him apart from the nearby traders in weapons and crafting supplies.
Jutak trades blades. Among the local merchants, his stock is distinguished by weapons rather than fishing or crafting supplies.
Hurklor supplies blacksmiths. His trade is one of two local shops focused on blacksmithing, alongside Jansen Underwood’s.
Fargon Mortalak is a superior armorer, selling armor in a district with separate shops for blades and blacksmithing supplies.
Blixrez Goodstitch sells leatherworking supplies.
Jansen Underwood supplies blacksmiths. His is one of two local shops devoted to blacksmithing supplies, the other run by Hurklor.
Glyx Brewright sells alchemy supplies.
Qixdi Goodstitch sells cloth armor and accessories, and can also mend worn gear.
Angrun is a herbalism trainer who teaches apprentices. He can also help unlearn talents and pet skills, and offers a second talent specialization.
Gringer is a wind rider master who offers travelers a ride. When threatened, he cries out for guards and an enraged wyvern appears to defend him.
Gyll is a gryphon master who offers rides and boasts that his gryphons are the fastest this side of Aerie Peak. When threatened, he calls for help and an enraged gryphon appears to defend him.

Nez'raz is the Durotar zeppelin master, proud of the sunny shores and crystal waters where he works. He compares his route to his brother Zapetta's post in Tirisfal and jokes that Zapetta is bitter about being stuck there and prone to whining.
Zudd is a pet trainer who teaches hunters to train their pets and offers pet untraining. He limits his help to hunters and their pets.

Ruzzgot is a goblin caravan driver whose caravan carried Velinde north before they parted; she was headed to Darkshire. He directs those seeking her to Clerk Daltry and warns that the jungle is dangerous. He describes his caravan as a shipping business.
A mechanical Venture Co. shredder.
A Murkgill forager, a humanoid that rends its foes in combat.
A Murkgill hunter who hurls throwing weapons at foes and flees to find help when badly hurt.
A Murkgill oracle who heals wounded allies with Healing Wave.
Murkgill Lord is the senior figure among the Murkgill murlocs. It casts Frost Armor while out of combat, marking it as a formidable presence within the group.

Murkgill Warrior is a fighting member of the Murkgill ranks. When reduced to critical health, it runs for help rather than pressing the attack, making survival and calling aid part of its battlefield behavior.
A Bloodsail Deckhand, a working sailor of the Bloodsail crew; when badly hurt in a fight, it flees to find help.
The Bloodsail Swabby is a shipboard crew hand in the Bloodsail ranks, a working sailor that casts a spell when wounded in a fight.

Booty Bay Bruisers speak as enforcers of neutral ground: they condemn bloodshed and warn miscreants to leave. In a fight, a Bruiser can cast a net to control an opponent, backing those threats with force.

Wharfmaster Lozgil oversees shipping in Booty Bay and can check the harbor's cargo records. In response to a Ratchet cargo inquiry, he reports boots as the latest outbound shipment and says no race parts appear in the records. For Revilgaz's business, he points the questioner toward the Baron.
Foreman Cozzle is a foreman who fights with spells, including one he casts when badly hurt.
Innkeeper Thulbek offers lodging and goods. He sees inns as places to rest after battle and share stories while making these new lands theirs.
Kurzen Mindslave is a humanoid held in mental enslavement; when hurt in a fight, it casts spells to defend itself.
Innkeeper Skindle offers lodging and goods. His greeting warns visitors away from the stove, joking that it has not exploded yet today, giving his inn a wryly hazardous welcome.
Senegal is a non-combat pet.
A cockatiel, a non-combat pet.

Oglethorpe Obnoticus is a gnomish engineering trainer who evaluates engineers’ work for gnome-oriented techniques. He also develops the OOX homing robot series, whose recovered prototypes spare him rebuilding time and manufacturing costs.
Nargatt sells food and drink to travelers.

McGavan is the Mithril Order’s Booty Bay contact for recruits seeking Galvan the Ancient’s smithing tutelage. He recognizes worthy candidates by their insignia and welcomes them with colorful approval.

npcs.name: Galvan the Ancient

records.text: Galvan the Ancient is an artisan blacksmith of the Mithril Order whose lessons join mining to smithing: he insists that an accomplished smith must also mine. He teaches the use of precious gems to strengthen enchanted work, and cites more than a decade spent in Alterac learning the lessons of truesilver.

npcs.title: Artisan Blacksmith of the Mithril Order

records.text: Scooty is Booty Bay’s chief engineer, responsible for calibrating the Transpolyporter 6000 to a passenger’s height and weight. He calls the contraption a pinnacle of goblin transport technology despite its history of explosions, and jokes that any future mishap will be quick and painless. His confidence comes with a warning: the trip to Gnomeregan may still have unusual side effects.

Se'Jib is a tribal leatherworking trainer who teaches the Tribal path in Stranglethorn Vale. His training material frames the craft as understanding and working with nature, and warns that choosing this path excludes the Dragonscale and Elemental specializations.
Ziggle Sparks sells holiday fireworks and invites visitors to browse the goods.
Rickle Goldgrubber is a banker who lets visitors reach their bank.
Knaz Blunderflame supplies engineering goods.

Grizzlowe is the shipmaster at the Maiden's Fancy berth in Booty Bay. He welcomes passengers aboard the route between the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor, mentions the ship's trip to Ratchet, and warmly praises Booty Bay clam chowder.
Auctioneer Kresky is an auctioneer who handles auctions for visitors.
Grimestack is a stable master who offers pet stabling and help recovering lost companions.
A Hakkari oracle who hurls Earth Shock at foes.
High Priestess Hai'watna is a humanoid priestess who fights with shadow magic and can heal.
Samantha Swifthoof is a humanoid who gives out tasks to willing helpers.

Squibby Overspeck is a zeppelin master who says he loves his job and jokes about slipping the boss a little coin. He wants Snurk reassigned to his port and asks visitors to put in a good word for him; he also points travelers to the Undercity zeppelin docked behind him.
Gluggle is a creature that splashes foes with acid.
Roloch is a humanoid who cleaves at foes in combat.
Rippa is a beast found in Stranglethorn Vale.
Kurmokk is a beast that can become enraged.
Verifonix, called the Surveyor, fights at close range with Pierce Armor.

Short John Mithril is a pirate who welcomes visitors to the Gurubashi Arena and delights in watching its fights. He advertises treasure in a chest on the arena floor and invites people to collect it, and calls for the bloodletting to begin. His arena business includes the Arena Master and Arena Grandmaster challenges: he asks for Arena Master trinkets and recognizes a competitor’s achievement. His pirate speech and enthusiasm make him an unmistakable showman of the arena.

Molthor, titled the Hand of Rastakhan, leads the Zandalarian contingent on Yojamba Isle. He speaks with urgent certainty about Hakkar’s return and says the island’s trolls may know how to stop the Soulflayer. During the Heart of Hakkar ritual, he directs his servants to banish the relic, then publicly hails Hakkar’s slayer as a hero.
A Zandalar Headshrinker, a humanoid found in Stranglethorn Vale.

Jin’rokh the Breaker is a troll of Mugamba who names himself envoy of Mugamba: Fist of Rastakhan. He speaks for the Zandalar Tribe, recognizing others’ accomplishments while acknowledging that their beliefs may differ. His dealings include warriors and heathens, and he assists those seeking pieces of Freethinker or Vindicator gear.

Al'tabim identifies himself as an envoy of King Rastakhan, with dealings among priests, mages, and warlocks. He speaks for Zandalar's struggle against Hakkar as a matter of the tribe's survival, and presents himself as proud of his people's history: he calls Kezan sacred Zandalar land and recalls how goblin trade princes drove his people out. His replies urge allies to fight Hakkar and promise them honor among the tribe.

Maywiki of Zuldazar is a Zandalar associated with the tribe's augurs and haruspexes. Maywiki explains that augurs seek divine insight to guide the tribe, while haruspexes draw wisdom from communion with nature and animals. Visitors can request assistance with augur and haruspex outfits, and Maywiki may greet them by saying they deal only with druids and shaman.

Falthir is a sightless Zandalar on Yojamba Isle whose sharp humor plays on his lack of vision and keen sense of smell. He says he can sense a hunter or rogue’s worth through their deeds, and speaks with pride of the tribe’s predators and madcaps. He offers guidance and rewards tied to their Zul’Gurub regalia, and welcomes those who have fought Hakkar’s forces as friends of the Zandalar.

Exzhal is a servitor of Rastakhan on Yojamba Isle. He warns that Hakkar’s enthralled high priests are channeling the power of the Zandalar’s sacred gods into the Soulflayer, and urgently calls for their plans to be stopped. He asks visitors to gather the channelers’ heads as proof of their part in that effort.
A humanoid Zandalar Enforcer in Stranglethorn Vale.
A captured Hakkari Zealot in Stranglethorn Vale.

Rin'wosho identifies himself as a trader of Zuldazar from the South Seas, bringing exotic goods from his homeland. He presents barter as something earned through standing with his tribe, and his dialogue connects Honor Tokens with tribal supplies, signets, and potent brews blessed by Zanza.

Vinchaxa is a servitor of Zanza who speaks for the Zandalar tribe's interest in the tribal coins of Zul'Gurub, which she calls Paragons of Power. She says the coins carry mojo, and trades one Honor Token for a set of three; the tokens buy special goods from Rin'wosho the Trader.

A Zandalarian emissary of Molthor’s expedition, this troll represents the group that traveled from distant islands to face the threat at Zul’Gurub. The emissary calls for heroes to enter the ancient troll city and later announces that the Soulflayer’s defeat has ended their peril.

Riggle Bassbait, the Fishmaster, runs Stranglethorn’s fishing tournament. He urges contestants to bring him 40 Tastyfish before anyone else to win the title of Master Angler; Jang buys fish from other participants after a winner is declared. Riggle jokes that he has been waiting for hours with nothing to eat.

Jang is Fishmaster Bassbait’s apprentice and helps handle the Stranglethorn fishing tournament. Once a winner has been declared, Jang offers silver for every five Tastyfish brought in, making a practical outlet for contestants who did not win. Jang calls the fish high quality and frames the purchase as a reasonable deal.

Fishbot 5000 is a mechanical fish-identification and reward unit. It makes whirring and clicking sounds, processes rare fish for Fishmaster Bluegill to catalogue, and says it was instructed to accept them in exchange for valuable Nat Pagle fishing accessories.
Servant of the Hand serves the Hand of Rastakhan.
Elder Winterhoof accepts the homage paid to him and offers a token in return. He recalls when his people hunted for glory and honor, and asks whether their lives have changed so much since then.
Elder Starglade looks to the stars for answers to earthly mysteries. She describes the stars of this age as beacons of hope and strength for the coming generations.
Auctioneer Graves is an auctioneer who handles auctions for visitors.
Auctioneer O'reely is an auctioneer who handles auctions for visitors.
Booty Bay Revelers are celebrants who sometimes gesture while out of combat.
The Drunken Bruiser is a rough brawler associated with drink.
Durik is a stable master who helps travelers stable their pets or recover lost companions.
Gremnik Rizzlesprang is a humanoid who will talk with visitors.

The Bloodsail Traitor is a former Bloodsail pirate seeking pardon from Revilgaz, but refuses to kill former crewmates. He offers to make replica bandannas from silk and red dye instead, and his speech is irreverent while condemning the murder of one's own crew.

Nemeth Hawkeye is a Farstrider who studies troll fighting styles and magic. He notes similarities between Bloodscalp and Amani tactics, investigates Bloodscalp magic for its potential against the Amani, and pursues what a totem may reveal about the water elemental Naias. He intends to send a recovered gem to Silvermoon for the magisters to study, reflecting his curious, strategic focus on the Amani threat.

Landro Longshot manages the Black Flame, a discreet concern that avoids factional entanglements. It deals in hard-to-find goods, gladiatorial combat and games of chance; Landro welcomes visitors by asking what they seek.
A hired bodyguard associated with the Black Flame, providing security for its operation.
Nizzle is a gryphon master who sends travelers on flights. When attacked, he calls for guards and an enraged gryphon appears to defend him.
A creature known as the Rocket Chicken, in the Black Flame's area.

The Stranglethorn Vale Flame Warden represents the Alliance's festival fire. Their greeting encourages people to honor fires in Alliance lands and calls Horde fires unworthy, urging visitors to desecrate them.

The Stranglethorn Vale Flame Keeper represents the Horde's festival fire. Their greeting encourages people to honor fires in Horde lands and calls Alliance fires unworthy, urging visitors to desecrate them.

Dread Captain DeMeza is a captain known as the Scourge of the South Seas. For Pirates' Day, she claims Booty Bay for herself and her crew until sunrise and invites visitors to celebrate with them; her celebration includes a way to become a Dread Corsair.
First Mate Hapana is a massive, taciturn crew member who grunts and directs visitors to Dread Captain DeMeza. One arm bears a tattoo of “MAGATHA” inside an arrow-pierced heart.

Ol' Chumbucket is part of Dread Captain DeMeza's crew and says the baron will regain Booty Bay after Pirates' Day. He credits himself and Cap'n Slappy with devising the celebration, and reminds visitors that dressing and speaking like pirates are both part of it.
Cap'n Slappy says he and Ol' Chumbucket came up with the idea for Pirates' Day. After Dread Captain DeMeza heard of it, the celebration took shape; Chumbucket identifies Slappy with DeMeza's crew.
A humanoid member of the Dread Crew in Stranglethorn Vale.
Dread Cannon is a mechanical cannon in the event area.
Nyuni is Hapana's pet and squawks pirate cries about keelhauling, walking the plank and scurvy dogs.

place_records.text: You are in Stranglethorn Vale, a jungle land in the Eastern Kingdoms where both the Alliance and the Horde hold settlements. The Horde keeps Grom'gol Base Camp, the Alliance holds Rebel Camp, and Booty Bay, a harbor of pirates and traders, is held by neither side. Trolls of the Bloodscalp and Skullsplitter tribes haunt the ruins, Bloodsail pirates raid the coast, and tigers and raptors roam the jungle.
You are in Zul'Gurub, the city of the Gurubashi trolls in Stranglethorn Vale. Gurubashi warriors and Hakkari oracles guard it, and High Priestess Hai'watna is its most dangerous named defender.

You are in Booty Bay, a harbor town in Stranglethorn Vale that is held by neither side. Fleet Master Seahorn commands the Blackwater Raiders from here and treats the Bloodsail Buccaneers as a serious threat. Bloodsail raiders hijacked a shipment of snuff, and Fin Fizracket lies gravely ill with Stranglethorn Fever in town.
You are in Lake Nazferiti, a lake in Stranglethorn Vale. Snapjaw crocolisks, sharptooth frenzies and Mistvale gorillas hunt along its shores.
You are in Wild Shore, a coast in Stranglethorn Vale where Bloodsail deckhands, warlocks and magi prowl the beach. Cowardly Crosby, one of the Goodstitch brothers, sells tailoring supplies here.

You are in Rebel Camp, an Alliance camp in Stranglethorn Vale. Lieutenant Doren leads the rebels, who once served Colonel Kurzen and now suspect a traitor among them. Brother Nimetz blames the ogre mage Mai'Zoth for Kurzen's corruption. Nizzle the gryphon master offers flights, and Corporal Bluth trades goods here.

You are in Nesingwary's Expedition, a hunting camp in Stranglethorn Vale. Hemet Nesingwary Jr. leads hunts for big game, and Ajeck Rouack trains hunters in tiger hunting while Sir S. J. Erlgadin teaches panther hunting. Young Stranglethorn tigers and river crocolisks roam the surroundings. Barnil Stonepot is still searching for the scattered pages of the novel The Green Hills of Stranglethorn.

You are in Kurzen's Compound, a camp of Colonel Kurzen's men in Stranglethorn Vale. Kurzen elites, commandos, medicine men and witch doctors guard it, and Colonel Kurzen commands from the Stockpile, the cavern complex at its back.
You are in the Ruins of Zul'Kunda in Stranglethorn Vale, ruins where Bloodscalp trolls roam. Bloodscalp mystics, scouts and headhunters are all found among them.
You are in the Ruins of Zul'Mamwe in Stranglethorn Vale, territory of the Skullsplitter trolls. Their warriors, berserkers, scouts, axe throwers, hunters and mystics roam the ruins.
You are in The Vile Reef, a reef in Stranglethorn Vale. Saltscale oracles, warriors, hunters, foragers and tide lords live among its waters.
You are in the Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound in Stranglethorn Vale, home of the Mosh'Ogg ogres. Warmongers, shamans, spellcrafters and maulers are among them, and Stranglethorn tigresses roam nearby.

You are in Grom'gol Base Camp, the Warchief's base camp in Stranglethorn Vale. Commander Aggro'gosh commands it and sends people to guard the supply route toward Stonard against raptors and ogres. Far Seer Mok'thardin works enchantments here, and Nimboya, a Darkspear from Orgrimmar, searches for his chief's lost son.
You are in Zuuldaia Ruins, a ruined site in Stranglethorn Vale. Bloodscalp witch doctors, berserkers and headhunters haunt the ruins, and saltwater crocolisks are among its dangers.
You are in Bal'lal Ruins, a ruined site in Stranglethorn Vale. Bloodscalp shamans, axe throwers and warriors haunt the ruins.
You are in Kal'ai Ruins, a ruined site in Stranglethorn Vale. Murkgill warriors, hunters, oracles, lords and foragers haunt the ruins, and a creature called Gluggle is among its dangers.
You are in Tkashi Ruins, a ruined site in Stranglethorn Vale. Bloodscalp axe throwers, warriors and scavengers haunt the ruins, and young Stranglethorn tigers prowl among them.
You are in Balia'mah Ruins, a ruined site in Stranglethorn Vale. Skullsplitter mystics, warriors and axe throwers haunt the ruins, along with jungle thunderers and Stranglethorn tigers.
You are in Ziata'jai Ruins, a ruined site in Stranglethorn Vale. Skullsplitter warriors, mystics and axe throwers haunt the ruins, and jungle thunderers are among them.
You are in Mizjah Ruins, a ruined site in Stranglethorn Vale. Mosh'Ogg witch doctors and brutes haunt the ruins, and a creature called Roloch is among its dangers.

You are in Jaguero Isle, an island in Stranglethorn Vale. Princess Poobah is held captive here by King Mukla, a Skymane king who commands the island's beasts, and skymane gorillas and jaguero stalkers roam the island.

You are in The Savage Coast, a coastal area in Stranglethorn Vale. A spirit healer is found here, but saltwater crocolisks, elder saltwater crocolisks, crystal spine basilisks, lesser water elementals, Stranglethorn tigers and lashtail raptors roam the coast.
You are in The Crystal Shore, a coastal area in Stranglethorn Vale. Silverback patriarchs, zanzil zombies and zanzil nagas haunt the shore, and Kurmokk and Gorlash are among its dangers.
You are in Crystalvein Mine, a mine in Stranglethorn Vale. Thrashtail basilisks and ironjaw basilisks haunt the mine, and a scale belly is among the creatures that live there.
You are in the Ruins of Aboraz, a ruined site in Stranglethorn Vale. Zanzil nagas, zombies and witch doctors haunt the ruins, and Zanzil the Outcast and Yenniku are among the notable creatures here.

You are in Ruins of Jubuwal, a set of ruins in Stranglethorn Vale. Zanzil nagas, zombies, witch doctors and hunters haunt the ruins, and Maury "Club Foot" Wilkins and Jon-Jon the Crow are among the hostile individuals.

You are in The Cape of Stranglethorn, a stretch of coast in Stranglethorn Vale. The Bloodsail Traitor, a former Bloodsail pirate, seeks pardon from Revilgaz and refuses to kill former crewmates. He offers replica bandannas made from silk and red dye instead. A spirit healer is also here, and jungle stalkers, naga explorers, panthers, gorillas and basilisks are hostile.

You are in Southern Savage Coast, a stretch of coastline in Stranglethorn Vale. A map written as orders to Bloodsail men tells them to hold a camp on this coast and wait for a signal from a southern command post before attacking. Bloodsail raiders and mages, along with basilisks, stalkers and naga explorers, are hostile here, and "Pretty Boy" Duncan is among them.
You are in Mistvale Valley, a valley in Stranglethorn Vale. Elder mistvale gorillas roam it in numbers, and Kurmokk and the Silverback Patriarch are among its hostile individuals.
You are in Nek'mani Wellspring, a spring in Stranglethorn Vale. Naga explorers are hostile here, and Lord Sakrasis is among the dangers.
You are in Bloodsail Compound, a Bloodsail base in Stranglethorn Vale. Bloodsail warlocks and swashbucklers are hostile here, and jungle stalkers are dangerous here too.

You are in Venture Co. Base Camp, a base camp in Stranglethorn Vale. Venture Co. geologists are the most common hostile here, along with Venture Co. shredders, mosh'ogg warmongers, shadowmaw panthers, and stranglethorn tigers and tigresses.

You are in Gurubashi Arena, an arena in Stranglethorn Vale where fights are held. Jungle stalkers, Bloodsail elder magi and Bloodsail sea dogs are hostile here, and Tethis is among the dangers. A spirit healer is also present.

You are in Spirit Den, a den in Stranglethorn Vale. Witch Doctor Unbagwa speaks with spirits here and offers to summon Mokk the Savage once given a gorilla fang. He asks to be guarded from the gorillas while he performs the ritual, and elder mistvale gorillas and Kurmokk are hostile here.

You are in Venture Co. Operations Center, a center in Stranglethorn Vale. Venture Co. geologists and mechanics are hostile here, along with sharptooth frenzies and snapjaw crocolisks, and Foreman Cozzle is among the dangers.

You are in Battle Ring, a ring in Stranglethorn Vale. Short John Mithril, a pirate, welcomes visitors to the Gurubashi Arena and delights in watching its fights. He advertises treasure in a chest on the arena floor and invites people to collect it.

You are in Yojamba Isle, an isle in Stranglethorn Vale where a Zandalar contingent is stationed. Molthor, the Hand of Rastakhan, speaks of Hakkar's return and the Soulflayer, and Exzhal, a servitor of Rastakhan, calls for the plans of Hakkar's enthralled high priests to be stopped. Rin'wosho the Trader offers goods and repairs here, and Jin'rokh and Al'tabim speak for the tribe.

You are in The Stockpile, an area of Stranglethorn Vale. Kurzen subchiefs, elites, witch doctors, commandos, headshrinkers and shadow hunters haunt it. A strongbox here holds a muddy note that points to a traitor among the rebels at the Rebel Camp.
